title: Attitudes of staff at a psychiatric clinic toward patients with borderline personality disorder before and after training in a disorder-specific psychotherapeutic modality
summary: The study is based on the observation that mental health professionals often harbor significant prejudices and face difficulties when working with people with borderline personality disorder. Several studies have shown that this is related to limited experience in working with these patients as well as insufficient training. Training in transference-focused psychotherapy, a disorder-specific form of therapy, is intended to reduce these reservations. This study aims to examine how the attitudes of employees at a psychiatric clinic toward patients with borderline personality disorder change following the aforementioned training, as well as to what extent these changes remain stable over time.

interventions.name: Clinic staff receive standardized training in transference-focused psychotherapy consisting of 2 sessions of 4 hours each. The content is taught by experienced instructors. The control group does not receive any training. At the same time as the intervention group, an identical survey is also conducted with the control group.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Employees at selected departments of the hospital who work in nursing, social work, psychotherapy, or the medical field.
Exclusion criteria:
Trainees and individuals under the age of 18, interns, patient service assistants, and cleaning staff.
